_meta.name: iss_baseline_profile
_meta.description: Multi-kingdom relative abundance vector for built-environment surfaces aboard a closed-loop spacecraft (ISS-analog). Derived from published ISS surface microbiome studies: Checinska Sielaff et al. 2019 (Microbiome 7:50), Singh et al. 2018, Be et al. 2017 (Microbiome 5:81), and Urbaniak et al. 2022 (Microbiome 10:100). Dominated by human skin and gut commensals with low environmental diversity due to HEPA filtration and closed atmosphere.
_meta.basis: Surface swab composite, 16S/ITS/shotgun metagenomic data from ISS Microbial Tracking studies (2015-2016)
_meta.notes: Closed environment with HEPA-filtered recirculated air. No marine or terrestrial environmental input. Microbiome shaped almost entirely by crew (max 6 persons) and cargo resupply. Elevated Staphylococcaceae and Enterobacteriaceae relative to Earth built environments. Radiation-tolerant taxa (Deinococcus) present at low abundance. Fungal community dominated by Rhodotorula and Aspergillus.
references: Checinska Sielaff A, et al. (2019) Characterization of the total and viable bacterial and fungal communities associated with the ISS surfaces. Microbiome 7:50. doi:10.1186/s40168-019-0666-x

Singh NK, et al. (2018) Succession and persistence of microbial communities and antimicrobial resistance genes associated with ISS environmental surfaces. Microbiome 6:204. doi:10.1186/s40168-018-0585-2
Be NA, et al. (2017) Whole metagenome profiles of particulates collected from the ISS. Microbiome 5:81. doi:10.1186/s40168-017-0292-4
Urbaniak C, et al. (2022) Microbial Tracking-2, a metagenomics analysis of bacteria and fungi onboard the ISS. Microbiome 10:100. doi:10.1186/s40168-022-01293-0

Archaea._note: Very low archaeal abundance in ISS environment. HEPA filtration removes most environmental archaea. Methanogenic archaea from human gut at trace levels.

Fungi._note: Fungal community dominated by Rhodotorula (Sporidiobolaceae) and Aspergillus. Penicillium and Cladosporium from cargo/air. Candida from human commensals.

Virus._note: Low viral fraction due to HEPA filtration and small crew population. Dominated by human-associated phages and endogenous retroviruses. No marine phages.
